title: This year has been a true test of my patience. The most important lesson I learned wasn't how to make money, but how to control losses. It has been a year of ups and downs.
author: Ok-Basil2753
selftext:
There were times when my account saw significant gains, but also moments when the situation took a sudden, unexpected turn for the worse. The biggest challenge wasn't finding profitable opportunities, but maintaining discipline when things deviated from the plan.  
Over time, I grasped a fundamental truth: trading doesn't mean getting it right every single time.  
I have never sought a 100% win rate. My goal has always been simple: control losses, preserve capital, and achieve growth through profitable trades.  
The market constantly tests one's emotions. Fear, greed, impatience, and overconfidence are the greatest enemies for most traders.  
There are no shortcuts in trading. You must understand your weaknesses, leverage your strengths, and repeat the process until it evolves into a mature, reliable trading system.  
After years of learning and trial and error, I finally found a rhythm that works for me: focusing on risk management and market trends, and making decisions based on a plan rather than emotion.  
My trading strategy is highly systematic, covering ascending triangle breakouts confirmed by volume, double top and double bottom patterns, flag (and pennant) patterns, and volatility contraction confirmed by ATR (Average True Range). Additionally, the strategy utilizes 5-day, 13-day, 34-day, and 55-day moving averages for multi stage trend verification, integrating analysis across short, medium, and long term timeframes.  
I share daily market insights for free in a stock discussion group, covering stock selection strategies, risk management, potential opportunities, and possible entry points.  
I won't promise you overnight riches; I simply want to share my experience and the journey that transformed me into a more disciplined and stable trader.  
If you are interested in learning, exchanging ideas, or gaining new perspectives on the market, feel free to leave a comment or send me a private message. I look forward to discussing these topics and growing together.
